messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Missing name in block fit_and_reporting.r:1058
parts:
Hi,
Just started seeing two errors, perhaps since updating roxygen2 to 3.1.0. (which by the way reports itself as packageVersion("roxygen") # -> 0.1.3

My package "umx" will still document() and install() without error. But when I run_examples(), I get this error...

> devtools::run_examples("~/bin/umx")
Updating umx documentation
Updating namespace directives
Error in stop(..., srcref_location(srcref), call. = FALSE) : 
  Roclet processing error in block fit_and_reporting.r:1058
Missing name in block fit_and_reporting.r:1058

I can't see anything wrong around that line (and nothing has changed.

Secondly, some functions with #' export in their roxygen are no longer exporting.

umx::print.dataframe
Error: 'print.dataframe' is not an exported object from 'namespace:umx'

despite this being the (unchanged) roxy code ahead of the function
#' print.dataframe
#'
#' A helper to aid the interpretability of printed tables from OpenMx (and elsewhere).
#'
#' @param x A data.frame to print
#' @param digits  The number of decimal places to print (defaults to getOption("digits")
#' @param quote  Parameter passed to print
#' @param na.print String to replace NA with (default to blank "")
#' @param zero.print String to replace 0.000 with  (defaults to "0")
#' @param justify Parameter passed to print
#' @param ... Optional parameters for print
#' @export
#' @seealso - \code{\link{print}}
#' @examples
#' print.dataframe(mtcars[1:10,], digits = 2, zero.print = ".", justify = "left")
#' \dontrun{
#' print.dataframe(model)
#' }


Any clues?

> exporting.
>
> umx::print.dataframe
> Error: 'print.dataframe' is not an exported object from 'namespace:umx'
That never should have been exported because it's an S3 method.

> despite this being the (unchanged) roxy code ahead of the function
> #' print.dataframe
> #'
> #' A helper to aid the interpretability of printed tables from OpenMx (and
> elsewhere).
> #'
> #' @param x A data.frame to print
> #' @param digits The number of decimal places to print (defaults to
> getOption("digits")
> #' @param quote Parameter passed to print
> #' @param na.print String to replace NA with (default to blank "")
> #' @param zero.print String to replace 0.000 with (defaults to "0")
> #' @param justify Parameter passed to print
> #' @param ... Optional parameters for print
> #' @export
> #' @seealso - \code{\link{print}}
> #' @examples
> #' print.dataframe(mtcars[1:10,], digits = 2, zero.print = ".", justify =
> "left")
> #' \dontrun{
> #' print.dataframe(model)
> #' }

What comes next? i.e. what sort of object are you documenting?

It's rather a bad idea to attempt to override an existing method.

Hadley

Thanks.

The problem was using @method (at least dropping that made the error go away
The offending code block was this (abbreviated):

# =========
# = begin =
# =========
#' confint.MxModel
#'
#' Implements confidence interval function for \code{\link{mxModels}}
#' @method confint MxModel
#' @rdname confint.MxModel
#' # blah blah blah...
confint.MxModel <- function(object, parm = "existing", level = 0.95,...){}
# ============
# = end code =
# ============

I can't see where in the code this error is generated, but it would be helpful to add this to the message

"Tips: If you are documenting NULL, check you have supplied a name. ",
"Else, if you are documenting an S3 function, check you have not used @method",
"(neither @method nor @S3method are needed in packageVersion(\"Roxygen2\") > 3.00) ", 
"Else check you've not done @name with no value following.",
" ",
"References ",
"http://stackoverflow.com/questions/14361616/s3-method-help-roxygen2 "
"http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7198758/roxygen2-how-to-properly-document-s3-methods/7199577#7199577"
